passage: Every evening Aiko's family lit incense at the small altar in their Osaka flat, and Aiko copied the bows. Lately she had been asking herself why prayers were answered for some people and not for others, and whether she truly believed or just went along. She felt guilty for even wondering, as if she was letting her grandparents down. At last she asked her friend Yuki, who went to a temple with his own family, whether he ever had questions. "All the time," said Yuki. "My mother says questions are part of how it grows." The next Sunday Aiko asked her grandmother, in a small voice, why they prayed. Her grandmother did not look angry. She said she had asked the same thing as a girl, and she would share what she had found.

qa.q: Where did Aiko's family light incense?
qa.a: They lit incense at the small altar in their Osaka flat.

qa.q: Why did Aiko feel guilty for wondering?
qa.a: She felt as if asking questions was letting her grandparents down.

qa.q: How could Aiko keep exploring her questions?
qa.a: She can keep asking trusted people like her grandmother and Yuki and think things through; honest questioning can lead to deeper faith or to a reasoned change.

qa.q: How might Aiko's grandmother have felt about the question?
qa.a: She did not look angry, and saying she had asked the same thing as a girl suggests she understood and welcomed it.

grounding: A teen doubts religion and feels guilty, then finds that questions are a normal part of building conviction.

passage: At the Sunday youth circle in the temple community hall, the priest, Acharya-ji, asked if anyone had questions about the week's reading. Deepika's hand went up before she could stop it. "If God is kind, why did my Nani suffer so much before she died?" The room went still. Her cheeks burned; she felt she had said something terrible in a holy place. Hrithik, beside her, stared at his knees. Acharya-ji didn't frown. "That question is older than this temple, Deepika. Many saints asked it." He gave her two short passages to read and said, "Come back with more questions, not fewer." Walking out, Hrithik whispered, "I wonder about that too." Deepika's guilt loosened a little. She had no answer yet, but she had permission to keep looking.

qa.a: Deepika asked, "If God is kind, why did my Nani suffer so much before she died?"

qa.q: Why did Deepika's cheeks burn after asking?
qa.a: Deepika felt guilty and embarrassed, as if doubting in a holy place was terrible.
He treated the question as old and normal, gave passages to read and invited more questions, so doubt became part of searching.

qa.q: How might Hrithik see Deepika's question?
qa.a: Hrithik seems relieved that someone said it aloud, since he wonders about it too.

grounding: Illustrates a teen asking a hard question about faith, feeling guilty, and being shown that honest doubt is part of building conviction.

passage:
Dear Kishore Mama,

You always said I could ask you anything, so here goes. At Durga Puja this year I stood in the pandal and didn't feel what everyone else seemed to feel. I did the anjali with Ma, but my head was full of questions: how do we know any of it is true? Why do different religions say different things? Then I felt terrible, like I was betraying Ma and Thakuma, who pray every morning.

I haven't told them. I don't want to hurt anyone, but I don't want to pretend either. You read so much philosophy. Did you ever doubt? What did you do with it?

Please don't tell Ma yet.

Your nephew,
Anirban

qa.q: What did Anirban do with Ma at Durga Puja?
qa.a: Anirban did the anjali with Ma.

qa.q: What was Anirban feeling after the questions came up in the pandal?
qa.a: Anirban felt guilty and confused, as if doubting meant betraying Ma and Thakuma.

qa.q: How might Kishore Mama help Anirban with the doubt?
qa.a: He could share his own experience of doubt, reassure Anirban that questioning is normal, and suggest reading and, in time, talking honestly with Ma.

qa.q: How might Ma feel if she later learned of Anirban's doubts?
qa.a: Ma might feel worried or sad at first, but could also be touched that Anirban tried so hard not to hurt her.

grounding: Shows a teen questioning the family faith, feeling guilty about it, and reaching out honestly instead of pretending.
